name: Quantum ESPRESSO (Quantum ESPRESSO Foundation)
origin_detail: Started in 2002 by merging three density-functional packages (PWscf among them) as an open initiative of the CNR-IOM DEMOCRITOS National Simulation Center in Trieste and partners (SISSA, ICTP and others). Since about 2011 the copyright is held by the Quantum ESPRESSO Foundation, a UK-registered non-profit company (no. 7542385).
openness_notes: GPL since the start (2002) and conceived as an integrated 'distribution'. Copyright is now held by a non-profit foundation whose members include SISSA, ICTP, EPFL, the Oden Institute (UT Austin), the University of North Texas and CINECA, so it is scored 4 (OSI licence plus neutral foundation governance).
risk_events: Core development is financed through successive, time-limited EU Centre of Excellence grants (MaX: H2020 824143; EuroHPC 101093374, EUR 8.5M total across several codes).
Small coordinating team (the user guide names two coordinators, Paolo Giannozzi and Pietro Delugas) supported by MaX and CINECA.
robustness: GPL code with foundation-held copyright and multi-institution membership in Europe and the US; installed as standard on major HPC centres (NERSC, LUMI, OSC) with NVIDIA and AMD GPU builds. Stable release 7.5 (19 Aug 2025).
physical_science_relevance: One of the two or three most widely used DFT codes in condensed-matter physics and materials science; the open alternative to VASP for plane-wave pseudopotential calculations, and a common engine for high-throughput workflows (e.g. AiiDA, Materials Cloud) and ML training-set generation.
openness_effect_assessment: Open licensing from the start let a national-centre code become a community 'distribution' with contributors across Europe and the US, and the 2009 reference paper has roughly 28,000 Scopus citations. The cost of openness is that it earns no licence revenue, so development is paced by EU grant cycles rather than sales, unlike its closed competitor VASP.
key_takeaway: Quantum ESPRESSO is the open, foundation-governed counterpart to VASP: comparable scientific reach (tens of thousands of citations) funded by European public research money and a non-profit that holds the copyright. It is a non-US comparator showing that the open model in DFT depends on public HPC programmes such as MaX/EuroHPC rather than on licence sales.
